issues.description: The no-argument constructor of the Common Person model differs in visibility between the template and the solution. The template declares a public default constructor (public Person()), while the solution's Person class has a package-private default constructor (Person()). This is a structural difference across artifacts and may confuse students about the required visibility for model classes used in REST request/response (deserialization) and the intended API of the Person class.
issues.suggested_fix: Choose a single visibility for the default no-arg constructor and make it consistent across template and solution. The simplest fix to avoid student confusion is to make the default constructor public in the solution (change 'Person() {}' to 'public Person() {}') so it matches the template and the common expectation for model classes used by Spring for (de)serialization.
